text: I am now financing a second vehicle through Wells Fargo. For the entire life of my previous loan, I would have to call them every month to correct them as to how the payments should be applied. My payment was about {$270.00} per month and I would send in {$500.00} to pay down the principal and save me some interest over the life of the loan. Month after month, they were applying the additional funds to future payments. I know this because, XXXX. ) the statement for the following month would show I only owed about {$25.00} instead of the regular {$270.00}, and XXXX. ) they told me this is how they processed payments. I referred them to their own paperwork which says that payments are ( in so many words ) applied first to interest, then any fees, penalties or late charges and the remaining amount to principal. Even after reminding them of their own wording and my XXXX years in the mortgage lending industry, they continue telling me that " these are their rules ''. They try telling me that once the future payments add up to XXXX months of advance payments, THEN they will apply any overage to the principal. If they do this to every customer that pays extra in hopes that they are saving interest, they are likely costing the public millions of dollars a year in undue interest.
